clue.text: Fellow going around quietly by river to get huge fish

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: the fellow goes around, so his word encloses the soft-music letter

parts.note: a fellow is a man
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A man circles a river softly, hoping to land an enormous fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge fish' reads as one phrase, but 'huge' gives OS (outsize) and only 'fish' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompanos are food fish of warm seas, related to the jacks.

clue.text: London area for the masses, not for the nobs

indicators.note: the posh letter is excluded from the word

parts.note: popular means aimed at ordinary people
U means upper-class, a British usage for the posh set

explanation.surface: A London district that suits ordinary people but not toffs.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class (Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U'); Poplar is a district in East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is a district in the East End of London.

clue.text: Burden makes one carry on grumbling, says Spooner

indicators.note: the first sounds of two words swap, as Dr Spooner did

parts.note: still in the sense of continuing to
to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: Constant complaining becomes a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: STILL MOAN with its opening sounds swapped becomes MILL STONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstone round the neck is a heavy burden or responsibility.

clue.text: A child, one of five like a 'dumb ox'

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets
as means like

explanation.surface: A child, one of quintuplets, likened to a slow-witted ox.
explanation.walkthrough: Fellow students nicknamed the young Thomas Aquinas 'the dumb ox' for his silence and bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval theologian was teased by classmates as the 'dumb ox'.

clue.text: Element above stretch of land — its form there?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: O is the symbol for oxygen
a zone is an area or stretch

explanation.surface: An element floating over a region, in a special form up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the element, oxygen; the answer is its three-atom form high in the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is an allotrope of oxygen, forming a layer high above the earth.

clue.text: Charlatan journalist brought into disrepute

parts.note: a charlatan is a sham, an impostor
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A fraudulent reporter has been disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shamed is to be disgraced, made to lose reputation.

clue.text: House's woman?

parts.note: the lady who receives guests in a home

explanation.definitionFit: A hostess is the woman who entertains guests at her house.

clue.text: Scottish official presenting one of his compatriots to the Queen

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scot
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A Scottish official introducing a fellow Scot to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A macer is an officer who keeps order in a Scottish court.

clue.text: Bring up girl on the hard stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
sinter is a hard mineral deposit from springs

explanation.surface: A girl turns to strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard stuff' suggests spirits; it is sinter, a crust round hot springs.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinter is to dig up from a grave.

clue.text: Shopping up north? Tricky situation taking a long time

parts.note: a mess is a predicament
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Doing the shops up north is a lengthy predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland, doing the shopping is called going for the messages.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish usage the word means groceries or shopping.

clue.text: Make a determined effort to give calves warmer environment?

definitions.meaning: idiom for making a real effort to improve
literally hoisting hosiery up over the lower legs

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means try harder; read literally it is hitching hosiery up the calves.

clue.text: Want to increase someone's fondness?

definitions.meaning: want in the sense of a lack
from the proverb that being away makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.definitionFit: A lack is an absence; the proverb says being away makes the heart grow fonder.

clue.text: Fatty stuff? It's wrong to swallow globule

indicators.note: one piece takes the other into its middle

parts.note: a sin is something wrong
a tear is a globule of liquid from the eye

explanation.surface: Someone protests that eating a blob of fat is a sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearin is a white crystalline fat, the main constituent of tallow.

clue.text: Course ending prematurely with smart lecture

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: a road is a course or route
to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: A course that stops early, accompanied by a clever lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a meal course (a roast), but it is a road, which loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting is a severe telling-off, a dressing-down.

clue.text: Majestic self-disclosure of a fairy to gangster?

parts.note: a peri (Persian fairy) announcing I'M PERI
Al Capone, the stock gangster

explanation.surface: A fairy confesses its identity to a mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means relating to an empire, hence majestic.

clue.text: Black market activity bringing in billion

indicators.note: the sale takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a sale is a market transaction

explanation.surface: Black-market trading brings in a billion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black market' reads as one phrase; in fact 'Black' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is a heraldic and poetic word for the colour black.

clue.text: Make savage insult come to light

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark
to arise is to emerge

explanation.surface: Making brutal insults appear.
explanation.definitionFit: To barbarise is to render barbarous or uncivilised.

clue.text: Toccata's misinterpreted not to be played legato

indicators.note: the letters are read in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A musical toccata performed wrongly, choppy rather than smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato notes are detached, the opposite of smoothly linked legato playing.

clue.text: Nurse provides cover for the end of her shift

indicators.note: the nurse's word wraps round the other letter

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A nurse covers for a colleague at the end of her shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a nurse's work period; it is the definition, a drift or tendency.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general shift or drift in a particular direction.

clue.text: They provide a platform for conveying story

definitions.text: They provide a platform for conveying story

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform
a lie is a story

explanation.surface: Newspapers give a stage for spreading tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Dailies are daily newspapers, which give a platform for tales.

clue.text: Bringer of message: vehicle on street has gone into school

indicators.note: the combined pieces enter the school's word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A message arrives because a car in the street has driven into a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of whales, a pod, not a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard is a card that carries a written message by post.

clue.text: Rude song is what you may hear from pirate

indicators.note: says the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: coarse means rude and an air is a song

explanation.surface: A pirate singing a vulgar shanty.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, especially of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Some girls in netball turned up for another game

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read upwards
only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: A few netball girls switch to a different sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes SINNET from girlS IN NETball; 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is another ball game, contrasted with netball.

clue.text: Fire that's cold and more full of burnt stuff?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ashier means more covered in or full of ash

explanation.surface: A fire that has gone cold and is choked with more ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' suggests flames; here it is the verb to sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss someone, especially an officer, from service.

clue.text: Members of congregation one saint, one hypocrite

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
Uriah Heep is the hypocrite in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: Churchgoers include a saint and a hypocrite.
explanation.definitionFit: The faithful are called a pastor's flock, so worshippers are this.

clue.text: Salt to represent sailor

parts.note: to stand for, so for means on behalf of
a mate is a ship's officer

explanation.surface: Old salt chosen to stand for a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like the old-sailor sense; it is the chemical meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Formate is a salt or ester of formic acid.

clue.text: Female dressing? It may spark something off!

parts.note: lint is a fabric for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: A woman's bandage might start a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Flint struck with steel produces sparks.

clue.text: A nice animator is at work, getting things into the Disney style?

definitions.text: getting things into the Disney style?

indicators.note: the letters are busy being rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A cartoonist busily turns everything into the Disney look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' reworks A NICE ANIMATOR IS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney is a famous American studio, so Disneyfying something is making it American in style.

clue.text: Resist work and put on airs

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to pose is to put on airs, behave affectedly

explanation.surface: Refusing to work and showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose is to resist or set oneself against something.

clue.text: Nags certain to be brought into line?

definitions.text: Nags certain to be brought into line?

parts.words: Nags certain to be brought into line?
parts.note: horses confirmed to run in a race, lined up at the start

explanation.definitionFit: Racing calls the horses that actually run in a race by this name, and they line up at the off.
